title: Of Offences Relating to the Army, Navy and Air Force
shortDescription: Offences by outsiders that undermine military discipline: abetting mutiny, assault on superiors, desertion and insubordination, harbouring deserters, and impersonating service personnel.

subHeadings.label: Mutiny and assault on superior officers

summary:
Chapter VIII protects the discipline and loyalty of the Army, Navy and Air Force. It corresponds to Chapter VII of the IPC (ss.131-140). The Gazette gives it no sub-headings; its ten sections fall into four groups: mutiny and assault on superior officers (ss.159-162), desertion (ss.163-165), insubordination and the scope of the Chapter (ss.166-167), and impersonation of service personnel (s.168).

The Chapter is aimed mainly at people outside the armed forces who interfere with them. Section 167 makes this clear: persons subject to the Air Force Act, 1950, the Army Act, 1950 or the Navy Act, 1957 cannot be punished under this Chapter, because their own conduct is governed by those service laws and court-martial.

Most offences here are forms of abetment. Abetting mutiny, or trying to seduce a soldier, sailor or airman from his allegiance or duty, is punishable with life or ten years even if no mutiny follows (s.159). If mutiny is actually committed as a result, the punishment rises to include death (s.160). The same two-step pattern applies to abetting an assault on a superior officer in the execution of his office: up to three years (s.161), or seven years if the assault is committed (s.162). Abetting desertion (s.163) and harbouring a deserter (s.164) carry up to two years; a deserter's spouse who shelters him is exempted, and the BNS now uses the word 'spouse' instead of 'wife'. The master of a merchant vessel on which a deserter is hidden through his neglect is liable to a penalty of up to ₹3,000 (s.165). Abetting insubordination, if committed, carries up to two years (s.166). Finally, s.168 punishes anyone who wears a uniform or carries a token resembling that of service personnel intending to be taken for one of them: up to three months or ₹2,000. All offences in the Chapter are cognizable except s.165, and none is compoundable. The serious ones (ss.159-162) are non-bailable, while ss.163-166 and 168 are bailable.

s.160 — mutiny committed in consequence: death, life or 10 years
Both cognizable, non-bailable, Court of Session
s.161 — abetting assault on a superior officer in execution of office: up to 3 years
s.162 — if the assault is committed: up to 7 years
Triable by a Magistrate of the first class
s.163 — abetting desertion: up to 2 years, or fine, or both
s.164 — harbouring a deserter: up to 2 years; spouse exempted
s.165 — deserter concealed on merchant vessel through master's neglect: penalty up to ₹3,000; non-cognizable
s.166 — abetting insubordination, if committed: up to 2 years
s.167 — persons subject to the Army, Navy and Air Force Acts are not punishable under this Chapter
Wearing garb or carrying token of a soldier, sailor or airman
With intent to be believed to be one
Up to 3 months, or fine up to ₹2,000, or both

fastRevision: Chapter VIII = offences relating to the Army, Navy and Air Force, ss.159-168; IPC Chapter VII (ss.131-140).
The Chapter targets outsiders; service personnel are dealt with under their own Acts (s.167).
s.159 — abetting mutiny or seducing from allegiance: life or 10 years + fine.
s.159 — the offence is complete even if no mutiny happens.
s.160 — abetment followed by mutiny: death, life or 10 years.
s.161 — abetting assault on a superior officer in execution of office: up to 3 years + fine.
s.162 — same, if the assault is committed: up to 7 years + fine.
ss.161-162 — triable by a Magistrate of the first class.
s.163 — abetting desertion: up to 2 years, or fine, or both; bailable.
s.164 — harbouring a deserter: up to 2 years; the deserter's spouse is exempted.
s.165 — master of merchant vessel, deserter concealed through neglect: penalty up to ₹3,000.
s.165 — the only non-cognizable offence in the Chapter; ignorance is no excuse if due to neglect.
s.166 — abetting insubordination, if committed: up to 2 years.
s.167 — no punishment under this Chapter for persons subject to the Air Force Act 1950, Army Act 1950, Navy Act 1957.
s.168 — impersonating a soldier, sailor or airman by garb or token: 3 months or ₹2,000.
None of the Chapter VIII offences is compoundable.
